issues.title: Dimension of the smooth counterexample
issues.failure_explanation: The prose declares that the example has m=1. The displayed map G has three components and the displayed inequality multiplier has three components, so the construction actually requires m=3. Thus the declared constraint dimension is incompatible with the construction it introduces.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the example is not well-typed under the paper's convention that G takes values in R^m and its multiplier lies in R^m. The example's calculation and conclusion remain intact after correcting the dimension.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace “m=1” by “m=3” in Example ex:failclarke. No other change to the example or its conclusion is needed.
issues.why_classification: The old source uniquely forces m=3: G has three displayed components and the displayed multiplier belongs to the same three-dimensional space. This is a transcriptional dimension error; correcting it makes the construction well-typed without changing or repairing any mathematical argument.

issues.title: Parameter space in the standing qualification

failure_location.quote: the MFCQ holds throughout the feasible set \(R(\param)\) for any \(\param \in \Rd\).

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The MFCQ is satisfied at any \((\param, \pvar) \in \graph R\)

issues.failure_explanation: The explanatory clause claims that the qualification holds on R(theta) for every theta in R^d. The old paper actually defines R with domain R^q and states the condition over graph R. With no identification of d and q, the R^d quantifier is ill-typed and differs from the parameter space established by the setup.
issues.overall_effect: The explanatory restatement of the standing qualification uses the wrong parameter dimension. The preceding graph-R formulation already states the condition correctly, so the formal results retain their intended support under the uniquely forced reading.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the explanatory quantifier “for any θ in R^d” by “for any θ in R^q.”
issues.why_classification: The parameter space R^q is fixed throughout the setup, R is explicitly defined on R^q, and the immediately preceding graph-R formulation already states the qualification correctly. Thus R^q is the uniquely forced reading, and the correction changes no assumption, inference, or downstream guarantee.

new_version_repair_locator.quote: the RCQ from Definition~\myref{def:mfcqCone} holds throughout the feasible set \(R(\param)\) for any \(\param \in \Rq\).

issues.title: Normalization in local boundedness proof
issues.failure_explanation: Let N_k be the norm of the original multiplier pair. Stationarity divided by N_k gives a right-hand side of -v_k/N_k. Equation eq:22122025a instead uses -v_k divided by the norm of (alpha_k,beta_k), which the proof itself establishes is one. Boundedness of v_k therefore does not make that right-hand side converge to zero, so eq:21122025a and the ensuing MFCQ contradiction are unsupported.
issues.overall_effect: The old proof does not establish local boundedness of the primal-dual solution map. The main conservative-adjoint theorem explicitly uses that local boundedness, and the smooth theorem is stated as its special case, so both conclusions are left unestablished until the normalization is corrected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In equation eq:22122025a, replace the denominator norm((alpha_k,beta_k)) by the original multiplier norm norm((lambda_k,mu_k)). Then explicitly use norm((lambda_k,mu_k)) tending to infinity together with boundedness of v_k to conclude that the right-hand side tends to zero. The resulting MFCQ contradiction proves Proposition prop:locboundp and restores its uses in Theorems theo:main and theo:mainsmooth without changing their statements or hypotheses.
issues.why_classification: As written, the proof makes an invalid limiting inference because the displayed denominator equals one. The correction is therefore substantive rather than a pure typo. Nevertheless, dividing the KKT stationarity equation by the already-defined original multiplier norm gives the required expression through a short, routine, source-supported calculation. This local repair establishes the proposition and its full recorded dependent chain with no weakening, new lemma, or change of proof architecture.
